tagline: World's largest bedding company transforming how the world sleeps
hero_kpi_rationale: Major strategic acquisition of $5.1 billion completed on February 5, 2025, transforming Somnigroup into an integrated leader in bedding distribution and retail with over 2,100 Mattress Firm stores in the United States

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total net sales for the fiscal year
kpis.description: Consolidated total revenue including Mattress Firm from February 5, 2025 (11-month stub period)
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by the acquisition of Mattress Firm

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross profit margin as percentage of net sales
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin, calculated as gross profit divided by net sales
kpis.signal: Gross margin expansion despite integration of Mattress Firm

kpis.name: Adjusted Gross Margin (non-GAAP)
kpis.explanation: Non-GAAP adjusted gross profit margin excluding certain items
kpis.description: Adjusted gross margin (non-GAAP measure) excluding special items related to the acquisition

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating income for the fiscal year
kpis.description: Consolidated operating income before integration expenses and adjustments
kpis.signal: Moderate operating income growth despite integration charges

kpis.name: Adjusted Operating Income (non-GAAP)
kpis.explanation: Non-GAAP adjusted operating income excluding one-time items and integration costs
kpis.description: Adjusted operating income (non-GAAP measure) excluding integration costs and special items
kpis.signal: Strong adjusted operating performance reflecting acquisition synergies

kpis.name: Mattress Firm Acquisition
kpis.explanation: Strategic acquisition of the largest US mattress specialty retailer
kpis.description: Acquisition of Mattress Firm, the largest mattress specialty retailer in the United States, completed on February 5, 2025 for $5.1 billion (net of cash acquired). Financed through $3.1 billion in cash and 34.2 million shares valued at $65.65 per share
kpis.signal: Transformative event making Somnigroup an integrated leader with 2,174 Mattress Firm stores

kpis.name: Mattress Firm Sales (stub period)
kpis.explanation: Net sales of Mattress Firm for the stub period from February 5 to December 31, 2025
kpis.description: Net sales of Mattress Firm from the acquisition date on February 5, 2025 to December 31, 2025 (11-month stub period)
kpis.signal: Mattress Firm contributes 47% of group revenue in stub period only

kpis.name: Number of Mattress Firm Stores
kpis.explanation: Number of Mattress Firm retail locations operated as of December 31, 2025
kpis.description: Number of Mattress Firm retail stores operated as a separate segment post-acquisition, with 73 stores and subsidiary Sleep Outfitters (103 stores) divested on May 1, 2025
kpis.signal: Mattress Firm brings major retail presence with 2,174 stores in the United States

kpis.name: Direct Channel Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of global sales through direct-to-consumer channels post-Mattress Firm acquisition
kpis.description: Over 60% of global sales come from direct channels (company-owned stores, e-commerce and call centers) following the Mattress Firm acquisition, with no single customer representing more than 5% of global sales
kpis.signal: Balanced omnichannel model with direct channel majority after acquisition

risks.title: Intense competition in the bedding industry
risks.score_rationale: The mattress and pillow industry is highly competitive with numerous competitors offering similar products and new entrants through direct-to-consumer models. Loss of market share and margin compression are material risks to sales and profitability.

risks.title: Supply chain disruptions
risks.score_rationale: Dependence on suppliers for raw materials and components exposes Somnigroup to disruption risks. Disruptions could lead to cost increases and reduce competitive capacity.

risks.title: Inflation, tariffs and macroeconomic pressures
risks.score_rationale: Inflation, potential tariffs and macroeconomic pressures on consumers reduce profit margins. While the majority of US products are manufactured domestically, limiting tariff impact, uncertainty remains regarding the duration and magnitude of future tariffs.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and data protection
risks.score_rationale: As a leader in omnichannel retail with a major e-commerce presence, Somnigroup faces cybersecurity risks including cyberattacks and customer data breaches. Such incidents could damage reputation and profitability.

risks.title: Labor relations and human resources management
risks.score_rationale: Deterioration in labor relations or union disputes could disrupt distribution and supply chain operations. The integration of Mattress Firm adds HR management complexity.

risks.title: Product liability and customer claims
risks.score_rationale: Somnigroup faces product liability risks related to mattress or pillow defects, product-related injuries, and customer claims. Such incidents could harm reputation and result in significant legal costs.

risks.title: Geopolitical and trade uncertainties
risks.score_rationale: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, trade wars and imposition of tariffs could disrupt operations and increase costs. Potential government shutdowns and changes in trade policies present additional risks.

risks.title: Mattress Firm integration risks
risks.score_rationale: The integration of Mattress Firm involves significant risks, including failure to achieve expected synergies, high integration costs, and operational challenges in consolidation. Inefficient integration could compromise the expected profitability of the acquisition.

ai_positioning.summary: Somnigroup does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. The focus is on product innovation, sleep technology, and retail operational excellence without explicit reference to AI.
